newsitem.title: PERU: Peru boy asks Japan PM to help free hostage father.
newsitem.headline: Peru boy asks Japan PM to help free hostage father.

text.p: An 11-year-old Peruvian boy has written to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto asking for his help on a special birthday present: the release of his father held for 51 days by Marxist rebels in Lima.

"I've never been without his hug on my birthday," Hugo Sivina Jr., who will turn 12 on Feb. 17, told the Channel Five television network on Thursday. The son of Peruvian Supreme Court member Hugo Sivina Sr. said he told Hashimoto "he was the only, the last person who could help me."

He said he had also written to Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and government chief negotiator Domingo Palermo. Neither has replied, "but I know they are going to reply by giving me the freedom of my father," he said.

Hugo Sr. has been held by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas inside the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima since Dec. 17. The rebels originally seized more than 500 guests but have freed all but 72, including two government ministers, congressmen, judges, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, about two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen and the brother of Fujimori.
